sources.title: EA SPORTS FC 26 Career Mode Deep Dive Pitch Notes
sources.notes: Primary authority for FC26 Tactical Visions, relaxed Player Role requirements vs FC25, mandatory Build-Up / Defensive Approach rules, and Silver/Gold Coach Role+ familiarity boosts.

conflictResolutions.conflict: FC25 required specific Player Roles per Tactical Vision; secondary matrices still list role-to-vision checkmarks.
conflictResolutions.resolution: In FC26, Player Roles are advisory Role Affinities (Layer 3) and never block selecting a legal FC IQ role for a position.

conflictResolutions.conflict: Official Career Mode documentation references 'Close Support' for Possession and 'Aggressive' for High Pressing, whereas tactical menus and secondary matrices frequently use 'Short Passing' and 'Extreme'.
conflictResolutions.resolution: Normalize 'Close Support' <-> 'Short Passing', 'Aggressive' <-> 'Extreme', 'Kick & Rush' <-> 'Kick and Rush', and 'Wing-Play' <-> 'Wing Play' while preserving both labels for transparency.

conflictResolutions.topic: Matrix Build-Up & Defensive Height vs Official Mandatory Rules
conflictResolutions.conflict: User-provided reference matrix marks additional Build-Up Styles and Defensive Heights as associated (e.g., Counter listed under High Pressing/Park the Bus/Kick and Rush; Deep listed under Possession/Wing Play).
conflictResolutions.resolution: Store official FC26 Career Mode requirements separately in Layer 2 (mandatory for verified vision compliance) and preserve all matrix Build-Up / Defensive Height cells separately as secondary reference affinities with explicit conflict flags.

conflictResolutions.conflict: Third-party guides propose numerical Defensive Line Height cutoffs (e.g. 1-30 Deep, 71-95 High).
conflictResolutions.resolution: Do not enforce unverified numerical line-height blocks in Layer 2; validate Defensive Approach label officially and treat numeric line height as advisory.

sources.title: EA SPORTS FC 26 Gameplay Deep Dive Pitch Notes
sources.notes: Primary authority for FC IQ canonical positions, new FC26 Player Roles (Ball-Playing Keeper, Wide Back, Inverted Wingback, Box Crasher), and Player Focuses.

sources.title: User-Provided FC26 Tactical Vision Compatibility Matrix
sources.notes: User-supplied secondary reference matrix mapping position-specific Player Roles, Build-Up Styles, and Defensive Heights across the 7 Tactical Visions (S, W, P, H, B, C, K). Publication date and patch completeness are unestablished; treated strictly as advisory Layer 3 affinity data.

conflictResolutions.conflict: Blank cells could be misread as banned roles or settings.
conflictResolutions.resolution: Blank cells represent 'not_associated' in Layer 3 advisory affinity only, never a prohibition. Positions/roles absent from the matrix (e.g., LWB, RWB, CF) are explicitly marked 'unknown'.

visions.description: Balanced football philosophy maintaining structural equilibrium across attacking, defensive, and transitional phases without extreme tactical commitments.
attackingPrinciples: Maintain balanced positional spacing across central and wide channels
Adapt attacking tempo to opponent block height and game state
Combine controlled build-up with vertical progression when space opens
defensivePrinciples: Preserve compact horizontal and vertical distances between lines
Balance pressing triggers with disciplined recovery shape
Avoid unnecessary tactical extremes that expose single zones
transitionPrinciples: Flexible defensive-to-attacking transitions based on numerical advantage
Measured rest defense protecting central counter-attacking lanes
strengths: High adaptability across diverse opposition setups
Low structural risk and predictable positional coverage
Broad role compatibility across varied squad profiles
weaknesses: Does not create extreme territorial dominance or overload specialization
Can struggle to break down disciplined low blocks without role-level adjustments

aliases.notes: EA FC 26 Career Mode Deep Dive also refers to Standard as Balanced.

visions.description: Width-focused attacking philosophy designed to stretch defensive blocks horizontally, create flank overloads, and supply dangerous deliveries into central areas.
attackingPrinciples: Maintain maximum attacking width along both touchlines
Exploit wide channels through wingers, wide midfielders, and overlapping fullbacks
Create 2v1 flank overloads and deliver crosses or cutbacks into dangerous box zones
defensivePrinciples: Protect wide channels during transitions when fullbacks advance
Ensure central midfield cover shields spaces vacated by wide progressions
transitionPrinciples: Rapid switches of play toward the weak-side flank on ball recovery
Quick wide progression to stretch recovering defensive lines
strengths: Stretches compact central blocks and isolates opposing fullbacks
Maximizes aerial, crossing, and pace threats on the wings
weaknesses: Exposed space behind advancing fullbacks and wingbacks on turnovers
Can become predictable if central box arrivals are isolated

officialRequirements.conflictNotes: Official FC26 Career Mode baseline requires Balanced or Counter Build-Up Style for Wing Play.

visions.description: Control-oriented philosophy emphasizing ball retention, close passing support, positional rotations, and patient progression through defensive lines.
attackingPrinciples: Sustain high-security ball retention with short passing combinations
Form passing triangles and positional rotations between lines
Progress patiently and exploit space as opponents lose defensive compactness
defensivePrinciples: Control match tempo through possession to limit opponent attacking phases
Maintain close support distances to enable immediate ball recovery after loss
transitionPrinciples: Structured rest-defense circulation rather than rushed vertical passes
Immediate short support angles upon winning possession
strengths: Controls game tempo and starves opponents of attacking volume
Dismantles disorganized presses through close triangles and central overloads
weaknesses: Vulnerable to turnovers in central build-up against coordinated high presses
Risk of sterile circulation if forward penetration and box runs are lacking

aliases.notes: Legacy FC24/FC25 Tactical Vision name mapped to Possession in FC26.

officialRequirements.conflictNotes: Official FC26 documentation specifies Close Support, corresponding to Short Passing in tactical menus; both are normalized as equivalent.

visions.description: Proactive territorial philosophy built on aggressive ball recovery in opponent zones, compact pressing traps, and fast attacking sequences after turnovers.
attackingPrinciples: Convert high turnovers into immediate vertical chances before opponents reset
Keep attacking and midfield lines compact to sustain wave attacks
defensivePrinciples: Engage opponent build-up high up the pitch with coordinated pressing triggers
Compress vertical distances between defensive, midfield, and forward lines
Restrict opponent passing lanes out of the defensive third
transitionPrinciples: Rapid direct vertical attack immediately after winning the ball high
strengths: Disrupts opponent build-up and generates high-value turnovers near goal
Controls territory and pins weaker ball-playing teams deep
weaknesses: High space exposure behind the defensive line against pacey runners
Demands strong coordination and can increase squad fatigue late in matches

aliases.notes: Legacy FC24/FC25 Tactical Vision name mapped to High Pressing in FC26.

officialRequirements.conflictNotes: Official FC26 baseline requires High or Aggressive Defensive Approach; secondary matrices label Aggressive as Extreme (normalized equivalently).

visions.description: Defensive-first philosophy prioritizing a deep, compact low block that protects central zones, minimizes attacking risk, and relies on disciplined recovery.
attackingPrinciples: Minimize high-risk attacking commitments and maintain numbers behind the ball
Select controlled, low-risk forward progressions only when clear outlets exist
defensivePrinciples: Organize a deep, tightly compacted defensive block around the penalty area
Protect central lanes and deny space between midfield and defensive lines
Enforce strict defensive discipline across all outfield roles
transitionPrinciples: Controlled outlet transitions after absorbing pressure without breaking shape
Prioritize immediate defensive regrouping upon any turnover
strengths: Extremely difficult to penetrate through central combinations or balls in behind
Effective for protecting leads or neutralizing superior opposition
weaknesses: Cedes territory and sustained pressure around the penalty area
Limited attacking numbers can leave forwards isolated when chasing goals
evaluationCriteria: Space allowed around the penalty area

officialRequirements.conflictNotes: Official FC26 baseline requires Deep Defensive Approach for Park the Bus.

visions.description: Transition-driven philosophy combining low-risk defensive organization with rapid vertical breaks into open space behind opposing lines.
attackingPrinciples: Trigger immediate forward runs behind the opposition defensive line after recovery
Prioritize direct vertical progression before the opponent reorganizes
Maximize efficiency in open-field transition situations
defensivePrinciples: Defend with low-risk compactness to draw the opponent forward
Force turnovers in middle and defensive thirds to open space behind the opposition
transitionPrinciples: Explosive defensive-to-attacking transition speed within the first 2-3 passes
Timely secondary support runners arriving behind the initial break
strengths: Punishes high defensive lines and aggressive possession opponents
Creates high-quality chances with minimal build-up exposure
weaknesses: Less effective against opponents who sit deep and deny space in behind
Can lose attacking fluency if initial vertical outlets are closed down

officialRequirements.conflictNotes: Official FC26 baseline requires Counter Build-Up Style for Counter Attack.

visions.description: Direct vertical philosophy leveraging long distribution, physical forward focal points, aerial/ground duels, and aggressive second-ball recovery to bypass congested midfields.
attackingPrinciples: Bypass congested midfield zones with direct long passes into forward zones
Use physical attacking presence to win initial aerial and ground duels
Swarm second balls immediately around target receivers
defensivePrinciples: Maintain balanced midfield positioning to contest second balls and long clearances
Stay compact enough to defend direct counter-clearances
transitionPrinciples: Immediate vertical release into attacking duels upon winning possession
Coordinated midfield push-up to capture knockdowns and rebounds
strengths: Bypasses elite high presses and congested central midfields quickly
Maximizes physical, aerial, and direct running profiles
weaknesses: Lower ball retention when initial duels or second balls are lost
Struggles if forwards lack physical/aerial competitiveness against dominant centre-backs

aliases.notes: Ampersand variant used in menus and guides.

officialRequirements.conflictNotes: Official FC26 baseline requires Balanced Defensive Approach for Kick and Rush.
